    "id": "essential-01-003",
    "title": "القلوب تحت تصريف الرحمن",
    "mainNarration": "عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما، أنه سمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: «إن قلوب بني آدم كلها بين إصبعين من أصابع الرحمن، كقلب واحد، يصرفه حيث يشاء». ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ: «اللهم مصرف القلوب صرف قلوبنا على طاعتك».",
    "reference": "[مسلم: 2654]",
    "commentary": [
      "جميع قلوب بني آدم، على كثرتها واختلاف أحوالها وما تخفيه من إرادات وأسرار، تحت سلطان الله كقلب واحد؛ لا يشغله قلب عن قلب، ولا يمتنع عليه منها شيء، كما أن خلق الناس وبعثهم جميعا لا يعجزه: ﴿مَّا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلَا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ﴾ [لقمان: 28]. وقد يستعصي على الإنسان إصلاح نيته وهو صاحب القلب، فيريد الإخلاص ثم تعاوده إرادة الثناء أو المال أو العجب، ويجد وحشة وانغلاقا لا يستطيع رفعهما عن نفسه، بينما لا يعجز الله تصريف قلبه من ضيق إلى انشراح، ومن غفلة إلى يقظة، ومن ضلال إلى هدى. ولذلك ابتدأ الحديث بخبر عن سلطان الله، ثم ختم بدعاء يعلّم العبد كيف يعمل بمقتضى الخبر؛ فمن عرف أن إصلاح قلبه وتثبيته بيد ربه توجه إليه، ولم يركن إلى نفسه أو إلى حال صالح مضى له. وإذا كان رسول الله ﷺ، مع منزلته وغفران ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر، يسأل تصريف القلب على الطاعة، فكل من سواه أشد حاجة إلى ذلك؛ والتحول من الطاعة إلى العصيان أو من البصيرة إلى العمى مصيبة تستحق شدة العناية والخوف. والحديث يثبت صفة الأصابع لله على الوجه اللائق بجلاله، من غير تشبيه بصفات الخلق ولا تكييف ولا تعطيل، مع الأصل الجامع: ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِۦ شَىْءٌ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ﴾ [الشورى: 11]. فكما يثبت له السمع والبصر من غير أن يكون سمعه كسمع المخلوق أو بصره كبصره، تثبت الصفة التي أخبر بها رسوله مع تنزيهه عن المماثلة؛ والاشتراك في اللفظ لا يقتضي تماثل الحقيقة، حتى في المخلوقات يختلف معنى المضاف بحسب ما أضيف إليه، كرأس الإنسان ورأس الجبل ورأس المال. وقد قال سفيان بن عيينة في نظائر هذه الأخبار: «هي كما جاءت، نقر بها ونحدث بها بلا كيف» [العلو للعلي الغفار ص156–158]. ولا يلزم من كون القلوب بين إصبعين مماسة ولا حلول في أجواف العباد؛ فالبينية في اللسان لا تقتضي اتصال طرفيها بما بينهما. قال الله: ﴿وَٱلسَّحَابِ ٱلْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ﴾ [البقرة: 164]، ولا يلزم أن يكون السحاب ملاصقا للسماء والأرض، ويقال بدر بين مكة والمدينة مع تباعدها عنهما، وسترة المصلي بين يديه مع انفصالها عنه، ويقال شعبان بين جمادى وذي القعدة من غير اتصال زمني بهما. فإذا لم يلزم الاتصال في هذه الاستعمالات بين المخلوقات، لم يجز إلزام الخبر عن الخالق بمعنى فاسد لم يدل عليه. وبيّن ابن قتيبة خلل حمل الإصبعين على نعمتين في هذا السياق؛ إذ لو كان المقصود أن القلب محروس بنعمتين لكان ذلك وحده تقريرا للأمن، بينما جاء الخبر جوابا عن الخوف ودليلا على الحاجة إلى التثبيت، كما تشهد أخبار حمل السماوات والأرض، وقوله تعالى: ﴿وَٱلْأَرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتُ مَطْوِيَّـٰتٌۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦ﴾ [الزمر: 67]. والإيمان بصفة الله هنا مقترن بالإيمان بتصرفه المطلق، فلا يستغنى بإثبات أحد المعنيين عن الآخر. ومعنى «يصرفه» يقلب أحوال القلب حيث يشاء، هينا سهلا لا يمنعه مانع؛ ووصف القلوب الكثيرة بأنها كقلب واحد يقرر كمال القدرة، فلا تثقل عليه كثرة الخلق. وذكر الطيبي في مناسبة اسم «الرحمن» أن توليه أمر السرائر من رحمته، فلا يكون اطلاعه عليها كاطلاع المخلوقين بعضهم على بعض. وفي لفظ «الإصبع» عشر لغات، وأفصحها كسر الهمزة وفتح الباء، وهذه ملاحظة في اللسان الذي ورد به الخبر، ولا تتناول كيفية الصفة. ثم جاء الدعاء «صرف قلوبنا على طاعتك»، و«على» هنا تحمل معنى دوام التقلب في دائرة الطاعة: ينتقل القلب من صلاة إلى ذكر، ومن صدقة إلى صيام، ومن علم إلى غيره من الخير، بدلا من أن يصرف إلى الطاعة مرة ثم يتركها إلى المعصية، كما بيّن ابن عثيمين. ومن مقتضى هذا الافتقار المبادرة إلى الاستجابة، كما قال تعالى: ﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ ۖ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ﴾ [الأنفال: 24]؛ فالحذر من رد الأمر أول وروده، ثم طلب الهدى بعد أن يحال بين القلب وبينه، يحول الخوف إلى مسارعة في الطاعة. ولهذا يسأل الراسخون: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْوَهَّابُ﴾ [آل عمران: 8]، وكان من دعائه ﷺ: «اللهم إني أعوذ بعزتك لا إله إلا أنت أن تضلني» [مسلم: 2717]. فهو سبحانه غني عن طاعة العباد، لا يزيده شكرهم غنى ولا تنقصه معصيتهم، ومع ذلك لا يرضى الكفر ويرضى الشكر: ﴿إِن تَكْفُرُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ عَنكُمْ ۖ وَلَا يَرْضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ ٱلْكُفْرَ ۖ وَإِن تَشْكُرُوا۟ يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ﴾ [الزمر: 7]، وإنما ثمرة الهداية للعبد وعاقبة الضلال عليه: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ لِلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۖ فَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَلِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا ۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِوَكِيلٍ﴾ [الزمر: 41]. فتعظيم القدرة هنا يفتح باب الدعاء والعمل والاستعاذة، ويعلم المؤمن أن يسأل الهداية والثبات حتى الممات."

All hearts are under the control of the Most Compassionate

‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him) say: “Indeed, the hearts of all the children of Adam are between two Fingers of the Most Compassionate, like one heart; He directs it as He wills.” Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: “O Allah, the Turner of the hearts, direct our hearts towards Your obedience”.

Sahih Muslim, 2654

All human hearts, however many they are, however different their conditions, and whatever intentions and secrets they conceal, are under Allah’s authority as though they were one heart. No heart distracts Him from another, and none is beyond His control. Creating and resurrecting all people is likewise never beyond His power: “Your creation and resurrection is only like that of a single soul[1].” [Luqman, 31:28]

A person may struggle to put their own intention right, even though it is their own heart. They want to be sincere, but the desire for praise or money, or a sense of self-admiration, keeps returning. They may feel lonely and closed off inside, unable to dispel either feeling. Yet Allah can readily turn that heart from distress to openness, from heedlessness to awareness, and from misguidance to guidance.

The Hadith therefore begins by telling us of Allah’s authority, then ends with a supplication that teaches us how to act on that knowledge. Whoever knows that their heart’s soundness and steadfastness are in their Lord’s hands turns to Him, rather than relying on themselves or on some good state they enjoyed in the past. Despite the Messenger’s exalted standing, and despite his past and future sins having been forgiven, he asked Allah to direct his heart to obedience. Everyone else is in even greater need of this. Turning from obedience to disobedience, or from insight to blindness, is a calamity that deserves serious attention and fear.

The Hadith affirms Fingers as an attribute of Allah in a manner befitting His majesty, without likening them to created attributes, describing how they are, or denying them. The Arabic report specifies two Fingers among the Fingers of the Most Compassionate. The governing principle is: “There is nothing like unto Him[1], and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.” [Ash-Shura, 42:11] Just as we affirm His hearing and sight without making them like the hearing and sight of created beings, we affirm the attribute His Messenger has told us of while declaring Him free of any likeness to creation. Sharing a word does not mean sharing the same reality. Even among created things, a word’s meaning varies according to what it refers to: the Arabic word ra’s can refer to a person’s head, a mountain’s summit, or financial capital.

Regarding reports of this kind, Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah said: “They are just as they are, we affirm them and narrate them without asking how.” [Al-‘Uluw lil-‘Ali al-Ghaffar, pp. 156–158; English: Mountains of Knowledge, Inheritors of the Prophets, pp. 180–181]

The hearts being between two Fingers does not imply physical contact or that Allah dwells within people’s bodies. In Arabic, saying that something is between two things does not require it to touch either of them. Allah says: “clouds which are held between the sky and the earth” [Al-Baqarah, 2:164] This does not mean that the clouds must touch the sky and the earth. Badr is described as being between Makkah and Madinah even though it is distant from both. A prayer barrier is described as being in front of the person praying—literally, in the Arabic expression, ‘between their two hands’—although it is separate from them. Sha‘ban can also be described as between Jumada and Dhu al-Qa‘dah without immediately adjoining either month. If such expressions do not require contact even when used of created things, we cannot impose a false meaning on a report about the Creator when the report does not indicate it.

Ibn Qutaybah explained why interpreting the two Fingers as two blessings does not fit this context. If the point were simply that two blessings protect the heart, that alone would convey reassurance. Yet the report came in answer to fear and as evidence of our need to ask for steadfastness. Reports about the bearing of the heavens and the earth likewise bear on this point, as does Allah’s statement: “On the Day of Resurrection, the whole earth will be in His Grip, and the heavens will be rolled up in His Right Hand.” [Az-Zumar, 39:67] Here, belief in Allah’s attribute goes together with belief in His unrestricted control. Affirming either meaning does not dispense with affirming the other.

‘He directs it’ means that He turns the heart’s condition however He wills, easily and without anything preventing Him. Describing all these many hearts as one heart establishes the perfection of His power: the multitude of His creation does not burden Him. A point transmitted in al-Tibi’s commentary, in connection with the name ‘the Most Compassionate’, is that Allah’s care for people’s innermost affairs is part of His mercy. His knowledge of their secrets is therefore unlike created beings discovering one another’s secrets. A note below clarifies this transmission.

The Arabic word for ‘finger’ has ten recorded pronunciations. The most eloquent is iṣba‘, with an ‘i’ at the beginning and an ‘a’ after the ‘b’. This is an observation about the language in which the report was transmitted; it does not describe how the attribute is.

The supplication then asks Allah to direct our hearts in obedience to Him. As Ibn ‘Uthaymin explained, the Arabic preposition ‘ala conveys remaining within obedience as the heart turns from one good deed to another: from prayer to remembrance, from charity to fasting, from learning to other acts of goodness. The request is not merely for the heart to turn to obedience once and then leave it for disobedience.

This dependence on Allah calls for a prompt response to Him. Allah says: “O you who believe, respond to Allah and the Messenger when He calls you to what gives you life[1], and know that Allah comes between a person and his heart[2]” [Al-Anfal, 8:24] We must beware of rejecting a command when it first reaches us, then seeking guidance after a barrier has come between the heart and that guidance. Such fear should move us to hasten to obedience.

That is why those firmly grounded in knowledge ask: “Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate[1] after You have guided us, and grant us Your mercy; for You are the Munificent Bestower. [Al ‘Imran, 3:8] Among the Prophet’s supplications was: “O Allah, I seek refuge in Your might—there is no god but You—from You leading me astray.” [Sahih Muslim, 2717]

Allah has no need of His servants’ obedience. Their gratitude adds nothing to His self-sufficiency, and their disobedience diminishes nothing of it. Yet He does not approve of disbelief and does approve of gratitude: “If you disbelieve, then Allah is in no need of you, but He does not approve of disbelief for His slaves. If you are grateful, He approves that for you.” [Az-Zumar, 39:7] The benefit of guidance belongs to the servant, while the consequences of going astray fall upon them: “We have sent down to you the Book with the truth for all mankind. Whoever follows the guidance, it is to his own benefit, and whoever goes astray, it is only to his own loss. You are not a keeper over them.” [Az-Zumar, 39:41] Reverence for Allah’s power therefore opens the way to supplication, action and seeking His protection. It teaches the believer to keep asking for guidance and steadfastness until death.

Quran translation note — 31:28
[1] The creation and resurrection of all of you are as easy to Allah as that of a single soul.

Quran translation note — 42:11
[1] In His essence, His attributes, or His deeds.

Quran translation note — 8:24
[1] A better life with faith both in this life and in the Hereafter.
 [2] Beware of rejecting the command of Allah when it comes to you, for Allah may not enable you to respond to his command afterward, as the hearts are between the two Fingers of Allah Who changes it as He wishes.

Quran translation note — 3:8
[1] ’Umm Salamah (رضي الله عنها) reported: “The Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray most by saying: “O He Who changes hearts, make my heart firm in Your religion” (yā Muqallib al-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ‘alā dīnik). When she asked him the reason for this, he (ﷺ) replied, saying: “Umm Salamah, know that every human’s heart is between two Fingers of Allah. Whoever He wills, He makes steadfast, and Whoever He wills He causes to deviate”. [Al-Tirmidhī: 3522]

    "completeRecords": [

        "title_ar": "إن قلوب بني آدم كلها بين إصبعين من أصابع الرحمن، كقلب واحد، يصرفه حيث يشاء",
        "title": "Indeed, the hearts of all the children of Adam are between two Fingers of the Most Compassionate, like one heart; He directs it as He wills",
        "hadith_text_ar": "عَن عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ قُلُوبَ بَنِي آدَمَ كُلَّهَا بَيْنَ إِصْبَعَيْنِ مِنْ أَصَابِعِ الرَّحْمَنِ، كَقَلْبٍ وَاحِدٍ، يُصَرِّفُهُ حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «اللهُمَّ مُصَرِّفَ الْقُلُوبِ صَرِّفْ قُلُوبَنَا عَلَى طَاعَتِكَ».",
        "hadith_text": "‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) say: \"Indeed, the hearts of all the children of Adam are between two Fingers of the Most Compassionate, like one heart; He directs it as He wills.\" Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) said: \"Allāhumma musarrif al-qulūb sarrif qulūbana ‘ala tā‘atik (O Allah, the Turner of the hearts, direct our hearts towards Your obedience).\"",
        "explanation_ar": "أَخْبَرَ النبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أن قلوب بني آدم كلَّها بين إصبعين من أصابع الرحمن كقلب واحد؛ يُصَرِّفُه حيث يشاء؛ إن شاء أقامه على الحق، وإن شاء أَزَاغَه عن الحق، وتَصَرُّفُه في جميع القلوب كالتصرُّف في واحد لا يشغله سبحانه شَأنٌ عن شأنٍ، ثم دعا صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: اللهم مُصَرِّفَ القلوبِ تارةً إلى الطاعة وتارةً إلى المعصية، وتارة إلى الذكر وتارة إلى الغفلة، صَرِّفْ قلوبَنا على طاعتك.",
        "explanation": "The Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) informed that the hearts of all the children of Adam are between two Fingers of the Most Compassionate, like a single heart; He directs it as He wills. If He wills, He keeps the heart firm upon the truth, and if He wills, He leads it away from the truth. His control over all hearts is like His control over one, as nothing distracts Him from any matter. Then the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) supplicated, saying: O Allah, the Turner of the hearts, sometimes towards obedience, sometimes towards disobedience, sometimes towards remembrance, and sometimes towards heedlessness, direct our hearts towards Your obedience.",
        "benefits_ar": "إثبات القَدَر، وأن الله يوجِّه قلوبَ عبادِه حسب القدر الذي كتبه عليهم.\nينبغي على المسلم إدامة سؤال ربه الثبات على الحق والهدى.\nالخوف من الله والتَّعَلُّق به وحده لا شريك له.\nقال الآجري: إن أهل الحق يَصِفُوْن الله عز وجل بما وصف به نفسه عز وجل، وبما وصفه به رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وبما وصفه به الصحابة رضي الله عنهم، وهذا مذهب العلماء ممن اتبع ولم يَبتدِع. انتهى. فأهل السنة يُثْبِتُوْن لله ما أثبته لنفسه من الأسماء والصفات من غير تحريف ولا تعطيل ولا تكييف ولا تمثيل، ويَنْفُون عن الله ما نفاه عن نفسه، ويَسكتون عما لم يَرِدْ به نفيٌ ولا إثبات، قال الله تعالى: (‌لَيْسَ ‌كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ).",
        "benefits": "Affirming destiny and that Allah directs the hearts of His slaves according to the destiny He has predetermined for them.\r\nA Muslim must continuously ask his Lord to keep him firm upon the truth and guidance.\r\nFear of Allah and reliance upon Him alone, without any partners.\r\nAl-Ājurri said: People of the truth describe Allah Almighty with what He has described Himself and with what His Messenger (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) described Him, and with what the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) described Him, and this is the methodology of the scholars who have complied and did not innovate in religion. End quote. So, Ahl-us-Sunnah establish for Allah what He has established for Himself of the names and attributes without Tahrīf (distortion), Ta‘tīl (negation), Takyīf (asking how), or Tamthīl (likening). They negate from Allah what He has negated from Himself and keep silent regarding what has neither been negated nor established. Allah Almighty says: {There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.}",
        "grade_ar": "صحيح",
        "takhrij_ar": "رواه مسلم",
        "grade": "[Authentic]",
        "takhrij": "[Narrated by Muslim]",
        "lang": "en",
        "link": "https://hadeethenc.com/en/browse/hadith/6331"
      },
      {
        "id": "3056",
        "title_ar": "اللهم لك أسلمت، وبك آمنت، وعليك توكلت، وإليك أنبت، وبك خاصمت، اللهم إني أعوذ بعزتك، لا إله إلا أنت أن تضلني، أنت الحي الذي لا يموت، والجن والإنس يموتون",
        "title": "Allāhumma laka aslamt, wa bika āmant, wa ‘alayka tawakkalt, wa ’ilayka anabt, wa bika khāsamt. Allāhumma inni a‘ūdhu bi‘izzatika, la ilāha illa ant, an tudillani. Anta al-hayyu alladhi la yamūt, wal-jinnu wal-insu yamūtūn. (O Allah, I surrender to You, I believe in You, I rely upon You, to You I repent, and with Your help I dispute. I seek refuge in Your Might. There is no god but You, that You do not lead me astray. You are the Ever-Living Who never dies, but the Jinn and humans die)",
        "hadith_text_ar": "عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضيَ اللهُ عنهما أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ يَقُولُ: «اللهُمَّ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ، وَبِكَ آمَنْتُ، وَعَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْتُ، وَبِكَ خَاصَمْتُ، اللهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِعِزَّتِكَ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ أَنْ تُضِلَّنِي، أَنْتَ الْحَيُّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ، وَالْجِنُّ وَالْإِنْسُ يَمُوتُونَ».",
        "hadith_text": "Ibn ‘Abbās (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) reported that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: \"Allāhumma laka aslamt, wa bika āmant, wa ‘alayka tawakkalt, wa ’ilayka anabt, wa bika khāsamt. Allāhumma inni a‘ūdhu bi‘izzatika, la ilāha illa ant, an tudillani. Anta al-hayyu alladhi la yamūt, wal-jinnu wal-insu yamūtūn. (O Allah, I surrender to You, I believe in You, I rely upon You, to You I repent, and with Your help I dispute. I seek refuge in Your Might. There is no god but You, that You do not lead me astray. You are the Ever-Living Who never dies, but the Jinn and humans die).\"",
